For Immediate Release

                                        Ameren Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results

        •   Third Quarter GAAP Diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS) were $2.42 in 2026 vs. $2.35 in 2025
        •   Third Quarter Adjusted (Non-GAAP) EPS were $2.42 in 2026 vs. $2.17 in 2025
        •   Raising 2026 Earnings Guidance Range to $5.35 to $5.55 per Diluted Share
        •   Establishing 2027 Earnings Guidance Range of $5.70 to $5.90 per Diluted Share
        •   Issuing EPS Compound Annual Growth Rate Guidance of 8% to 10% for 2027 through 2031, using the 2027 Guidance
            Midpoint as the Base


ST. LOUIS (November 5, 2026) — Ameren Corporation (NYSE: AEE) today announced third quarter 2026 net income attributable to common
shareholders in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) of $676 million, or $2.42 per diluted share, compared to third
quarter 2025 GAAP net income of $640 million, or $2.35 per diluted share. Excluding a third quarter 2025 tax benefit described in the table
below, Ameren recorded third quarter 2025 adjusted (non-GAAP) net income attributable to common shareholders of $592 million, or $2.17 per
diluted share.

Third quarter 2026 results, compared to adjusted third quarter 2025 results, reflected increased earnings on infrastructure investments to
improve system reliability, resiliency and service quality, increased earnings on investments in innovative energy technologies, and higher
Ameren Missouri electric retail sales, primarily driven by warmer temperatures. These positive contributions were partially offset by higher
Ameren Missouri operations and maintenance expenses, primarily driven by increased reliability-focused tree trimming and energy center
maintenance. Finally, the earnings per diluted share comparison reflected higher weighted-average basic common shares outstanding in the
third quarter of 2026.

"Our third-quarter results were driven by continued execution of our strategy and disciplined investment in critical energy infrastructure to deliver
reliable energy for our customers at the lowest cost possible," said Martin J. Lyons, Jr., chairman, president and chief executive officer of Ameren
Corporation. "We are well positioned to meet growing energy needs, support significant economic development across our region and deliver
lasting benefits for the customers and communities we serve."

 Ameren recorded GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, of $1,347 million, or
$4.83 per diluted share, compared to GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, of
$1,204 million, or $4.43 per diluted share. Excluding a third quarter 2025 tax benefit described below, Ameren recorded adjusted (non-GAAP)
net income attributable to common shareholders of $1,156 million, or $4.25 per diluted share for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
Results for the first nine months of 2026, compared to adjusted results for the first nine months of 2025, reflected higher earnings on
infrastructure investments to improve system reliability, resiliency and service quality, higher earnings on investments in innovative energy
technologies and higher Ameren Missouri electric retail sales, driven in part by warmer summer temperatures. These positive contributions were
partially offset by higher Ameren Missouri operations and maintenance expenses, primarily driven by increased reliability-focused tree trimming
and energy center maintenance, and higher interest expense. Finally, the earnings per diluted share comparison reflected higher weighted-
average basic common shares outstanding in 2026.

Earnings and Rate Base Guidance

Today, Ameren is raising its 2026 earnings guidance range to $5.35 to $5.55 from $5.25 to $5.45 per share. Further, Ameren expects 2027
diluted earnings per share to be in a range of $5.70 to $5.90 per share, representing 8.4% growth from the original 2026 guidance midpoint.


"Our strong year-to-date performance gives us confidence to raise our 2026 earnings guidance. As we look to 2027, we’ll continue executing our
strategy and investing in energy infrastructure to deliver long-term value for customers and shareholders,” Lyons said.

Ameren expects diluted earnings per share to grow at an 8% to 10% compound annual rate from 2027 through 2031, using the 2027 guidance
range midpoint of $5.80 per share as the base. Ameren's multi-year earnings growth is expected to be driven by $38.1 billion of planned
infrastructure investments underpinning projected rate base growth of approximately 13.3% compounded annually from 2026 through 2031.
Ameren expects to continue to grow its common dividend annually, with a payout ratio ranging between 45% and 55% of annual earnings per
share.

“Our updated long-term outlook reflects the significant investments needed to serve growing demand from large customers and support
economic growth across our region. By strengthening and expanding the energy grid, we




                                                                      Page 2 of 6
 can meet that demand while delivering lasting value for our customers, communities and shareholders. We are well positioned to execute our
strategy while keeping our customers at the center of everything we do,” Lyons said.

Earnings guidance for 2026 assumes normal temperatures for the last three months of the year, and earnings guidance for 2027 and multi-year
earnings growth expectations assume normal temperatures. Earnings guidance for 2026 and 2027 and multi-year earnings growth expectations
are subject to the effects of, among other things: regulatory, judicial and legislative actions; energy center and energy transmission and
distribution operations; energy, economic, capital and credit market conditions; customer usage; severe storms; returns on market-based and
other investments; unusual or otherwise unexpected gains or losses; and other risks and uncertainties outlined, or referred to, in the Forward-
looking Statements section of this press release.


Ameren Missouri Segment Results

Ameren Missouri third quarter 2026 earnings were $582 million, compared to third quarter 2025 earnings of $518 million. The year-over-year
increase reflected earnings on increased infrastructure investments, higher electric retail sales, primarily driven by warmer weather, and lower
income tax expense due, in part, to timing differences. These positive factors were partially offset by higher operations and maintenance
expenses, primarily driven by increased reliability-focused tree trimming and energy center maintenance, and higher interest expense.

Ameren Transmission Segment Results

Ameren Transmission third quarter 2026 earnings were $110 million, compared to third quarter 2025 GAAP and adjusted earnings of $151
million and $103 million, respectively. Adjusted earnings in 2025 excluded the tax benefit described in the table above. The year-over-year
comparison reflected earnings on increased infrastructure investments.

Ameren Illinois Electric Distribution Segment Results

Ameren Illinois Electric Distribution third quarter 2026 earnings were $72 million, compared to third quarter 2025 earnings of $57 million. The
year-over-year increase reflected earnings on increased infrastructure investments.

Ameren Illinois Natural Gas Segment Results


Ameren Illinois Natural Gas third quarter 2026 loss was $7 million, compared to third quarter 2025 loss of $13 million. The year-over-year
comparison reflected increased infrastructure investments included in natural gas service rates that became effective December 2, 2025.

Ameren Parent Results (includes items not reported in a business segment)

Ameren Parent third quarter 2026 loss was $81 million, compared to a third quarter 2025 loss of $73 million. The year-over-year comparison
primarily reflected higher income tax expense due, in part, to timing differences, and higher interest expense, partially offset by higher earnings
from investments in innovative energy technologies.

 Analyst Conference Call

Ameren will conduct a conference call for financial analysts at 9 a.m. Central Time on Friday, November 6, 2026, to discuss third quarter 2026
earnings, earnings guidance and other matters. Investors, the news media and the public may listen to a live broadcast of the call at
AmerenInvestors.com by clicking on "Webcast" under "Latest Quarterly Results," where an accompanying slide presentation will also be
available. The conference call and presentation will be archived in the “Investors” section of the website under “Quarterly Earnings.”

About Ameren

St. Louis-based Ameren Corporation powers the quality of life for 2.5 million electric customers and more than 900,000 natural gas customers in
a 64,000-square-mile area through its Ameren Missouri and Ameren Illinois rate-regulated utility subsidiaries. Ameren Illinois provides electric
transmission and distribution service and natural gas distribution service. Ameren Missouri provides electric generation, transmission and
distribution service, as well as natural gas distribution service. Ameren Transmission Company of Illinois develops, owns and operates rate-
regulated regional electric transmission projects in the Midcontinent Independent System Operator (MISO), Inc. For more information, visit
Ameren.com, or follow us at @AmerenCorp, Facebook.com/AmerenCorp, or LinkedIn.com/company/Ameren.

Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

In this release, Ameren has presented adjusted earnings and adjusted earnings per share, which are non-GAAP measures and may not be
comparable to those of other companies. A reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP information is included in this release. Generally, adjusted
earnings or losses include earnings or losses attributable to Ameren common shareholders and exclude income or loss from significant discrete
items that management does not consider representative of ongoing earnings. Ameren uses adjusted earnings internally for financial planning
and for analysis of performance. Ameren also uses adjusted earnings as the primary performance measurement when communicating with
analysts and investors regarding our earnings results and outlook, as the company believes that adjusted earnings allow the company to more
accurately compare its ongoing performance across periods. In providing adjusted earnings guidance, there could be differences between
adjusted earnings and earnings prepared in accordance with GAAP as a result of our treatment of certain items.
